instruction: I'm thinking of adding some living space to my home. What are my options?
reply: Bring the things that make the room theirs and give you something to do together: a framed photo, a small photo album, their own blanket or cardigan, a radio or a favourite mug, and a newspaper or a box of their usual sweets. Check what the room already has and what the home allows before you buy anything, and take one thing a visit rather than a car load - it is the visits, not the stuff, that make the room theirs.

instruction: I have a lot of homework to do and I'm feeling overwhelmed. Can you help me organize it?
reply: Homework earns its place in small doses: about ten minutes a night in the first years of primary, half an hour by the end of it and an hour or so at secondary, and the evidence for it is weakest for the youngest children. What makes it work is the same each night - a fixed time, a clear table, and you nearby without taking over.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm looking for new ways to engage my students in the classroom. Have you heard of game-based learning?
reply: Ask in person after class with one specific thing ("I get the formula but I can't do the last question on the sheet"), and say what you've already tried. Teachers help far more often than students expect, and an email the same day saying thank you makes them remember you next time.

instruction: I'm interested in track and field events. What's the most popular one?
reply: The Grand Slams are the four biggest tournaments: the Australian Open in January, the French Open at Roland-Garros on clay, Wimbledon on grass, and the US Open. Winning all four in the same year is a calendar Grand Slam - Rod Laver did it in 1969 and Steffi Graf in 1988.

instruction: I'm looking for educational resources to learn about history. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Start with *The Rest Is History* (two funny historians), *Desert Island Discs* for people talking about their lives, or *Casefile* if you want a true crime story told straight. Tell me what you usually listen to and I'll aim closer.

instruction: I'm trying to get more exercise, so I've been thinking about walking more.
reply: Yes: it builds flexibility and balance and strengthens the muscles that hold you up, and it counts as exercise, though the heart and lungs get less from it than from a brisk walk. Two or three sessions a week is where the change shows, and a weekly class plus ten minutes at home most days is the usual way people keep it up.

instruction: I'm looking for information about famous artists. Can you tell me about Vincent van Gogh?
reply: Vincent van Gogh (1853-1890) was a Dutch painter whose The Starry Night, Sunflowers and self-portraits are among the most recognised pictures in the world. He sold almost nothing in his lifetime, cut off part of his own ear in 1888, and died at 37, with his fame arriving afterwards.

instruction: I'm worried about pollution in our oceans. Is it really a big problem?
reply: Rain wears minerals out of rocks and carries them to the sea, and when the water evaporates the salt stays behind. Rivers keep adding a little, so the sea has become salty over hundreds of millions of years.

instruction: I'm learning to code and I was wondering what programming languages are used for web development.
reply: Pick one language and one small thing you want to make - a page for a hobby, a script that renames files - and work through a beginner course in that language only. Python or JavaScript is the usual start; HTML and CSS first if you want to see a page you build in a browser.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm looking for an online learning platform to use with my students. Have you heard of Google Classroom?
reply: Ask in person after class with one specific thing ("I get the formula but I can't do the last question on the sheet"), and say what you've already tried. Teachers help far more often than students expect, and an email the same day saying thank you makes them remember you next time.

instruction: I'm learning about endangered species. What is biodiversity?
reply: A species is a group of living things that can breed together and produce fertile young: dogs are one species, and a horse and a donkey are different species because their mule offspring cannot have young. Members of a species share most of their genes.

instruction: I'm a beginner runner and I'm trying to improve my technique. What's the most important thing to focus on?
reply: Start with run-walk: three minutes of easy running, two minutes of walking, five times, three days a week, and add a minute of running each week. Build up for six weeks before you add speed, keep every run slow enough to talk, and expect the first fortnight to feel harder than it looks.

instruction: I'm learning about renewable and non-renewable resources in school. What's the difference between the two?
reply: Both are state schools and free to attend. A maintained school is run by the local authority; an academy is funded directly by the government, sets its own curriculum and admissions, and is run by a trust.

instruction: I'm trying to get more exercise, so I was thinking of starting a walk-to-work initiative in my neighborhood. Do you think it's a good idea?
reply: Yes: it builds flexibility and balance and strengthens the muscles that hold you up, and it counts as exercise, though the heart and lungs get less from it than from a brisk walk. Two or three sessions a week is where the change shows, and a weekly class plus ten minutes at home most days is the usual way people keep it up.

instruction: I'm looking for educational resources for my kids. Do you know any good websites for interactive simulations?
reply: Ask three or four people who have just passed and book a single lesson with the one they liked most - a good instructor is the thing that makes lessons worth the money, and one lesson tells you more than any advert. Look for someone approved by the DVSA (an ADI badge on the windscreen), a quiet manner, and a lesson plan rather than being driven round for two hours.

instruction: I'm thinking of upgrading my computer's operating system. What's the difference between Windows and macOS?
reply: The operating system is the layer between the programs and the machine: Windows, macOS, Android and iOS are the four you meet. It manages the files, the screen and the battery, and it decides which apps can run, which is why an app that has stopped being updated eventually stops opening on a new version.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a new puppy and I'm wondering how I can help it get along with my other pets.
reply: Start further away than you think you need to: a distance where he can see a dog and still take a treat, then let the other dog pass and walk on. Repeat that a few times a week, never let dogs rush up nose to nose on the lead, and stay calm yourself because the lead tightens when you brace and that tells him there is something to fear.

instruction: What causes the seasons to change?
reply: Seasons come from the Earth's 23.5-degree tilt, not from how close it is to the sun. When your half of the planet leans towards the sun you get summer: longer days and more direct light.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my social studies homework. What is geography?
reply: Keep the sentences short and the geography simple: who is where, what is in reach, and what each of them wants in the next ten seconds. Two or three blows that land badly, one thing that goes wrong - a foot in a puddle, a hand that will not close - and a cost at the end, because a fight nobody loses anything in reads like a dance.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed and I'm looking for some relaxation techniques. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Pick the smallest physical thing first, because stress lives in the body: a slow breath out for longer than the breath in, a ten-minute walk, or a glass of water and something to eat if you have skipped a meal. Then write down what is actually on your plate and cut one thing or ask for one deadline to move.

instruction: I'm learning about food chains in school. What's the difference between a carnivore, an herbivore, and an omnivore?
reply: A food chain is the line of who eats whom, starting with a plant that makes its own food and ending with a predator. Energy is lost at every step, which is why top predators are few and a chain rarely has more than four or five links.

instruction: I want to cook healthier meals, but I'm not sure where to start.
reply: You can eat well without cooking if you build the plate from the shop: a bag of salad or a punnet of tomatoes, ready-cooked chicken or a tin of tuna or chickpeas, and bread, couscous or a microwave pouch of rice. Frozen veg straight from the microwave is the cheapest half-plate of vegetables there is, and a pot of yogurt with fruit is pudding.

instruction: I'm trying to stay hydrated. What are some water-rich foods I can eat?
reply: Sip small amounts of water or a rehydration drink often rather than a glass at once, and eat something dry and plain - toast, crackers, a plain biscuit - before you get up if mornings are the worst. Ginger, in tea or a biscuit, settles some people.

instruction: It's raining outside, what should I wear?
reply: Dress for standing about outdoors: shorts or jeans and a light top, with a jumper for when the sun goes in. Leave the white things and the dry-clean-only at home, because there's smoke, grass and someone with a ketchup bottle.

instruction: I'm starting a vegetable garden. What are some easy vegetables to grow?
reply: Grow what gives you a lot from a little: salad leaves, radishes, spring onions, dwarf beans, cherry tomatoes, chillies, one courgette plant, herbs in a pot by the door, and strawberries in a basket. Go upwards where you can - beans and cucumbers up a frame, tomatoes in a grow bag - and sow a few seeds every three weeks rather than everything at once, so you eat from June to October instead of facing a glut in August.

instruction: I'm planning a vacation to Europe and I'm looking for suggestions on historical landmarks to visit.
reply: Berlin has about 3.8 million people, the biggest city in Germany and about eight times the size of Frankfurt.

instruction: I'm having trouble communicating with my family about important decisions. Do you have any tips?
reply: Send an agenda 24 hours before with the decision you need, and start with it. If there isn't a decision to make, it's an email; if it's only updates, make it a 10-minute stand-up.

instruction: I'm learning about plants in school. Do plants respond to their environment?
reply: Plants use sunlight to turn carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil into sugar, which is their food, and they release oxygen as a by-product. The green chlorophyll in their leaves captures the light that powers it.

instruction: I'm looking for a new way to cook my favorite beef stew. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Stews, curries, chilli, bolognese, soup, lasagne and shepherd's pie all freeze well and come back the same; cook them a bit under and freeze in portions flat in bags so they thaw fast. Leave out potatoes cooked in a stew, pasta and rice cooked in it, and add fresh pasta, rice or a jacket potato on the day.

instruction: I'm feeling unwell and I'm not sure if I should go to the doctor.
reply: Feeling under the weather means a bit unwell - off colour, not seriously ill. What is wrong - sore throat, tired, sick?

instruction: I'm learning to play the guitar. What's the difference between a chord and a scale?
reply: Ten to fifteen minutes a day beats one long session a week: learn the four chords G, C, D and Em first, then play songs that use them, since songs keep you going where scales do not. Most people can strum through a simple song in two or three months that way; sore fingertips for the first fortnight are normal.

instruction: I'm a huge music fan. I've been to a few concerts and I was wondering what it's like backstage.
reply: Most theatres are smart casual now: trousers or dark jeans and a nice top, with a jacket if it's a big West End or opera night. Nobody minds as long as you're warm and not in shorts.

instruction: I love going to the mall to look at the seasonal displays. What's your favorite season for window shopping?
reply: Seasons stay lower case: spring, summer, autumn, winter. Days and months take a capital - Monday, January - and so do holidays, as in Christmas.

instruction: I'm looking for free online educational resources for my kids. Do you know any good websites?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm worried about climate change. What's the main cause?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

instruction: I'm planning a retirement party for my mom. What are some common family celebrations?
reply: Two lines is plenty unless it is family: "Merry Christmas - hope the year has been kind to you and the next one is better." Add a specific thing you remember from the year for anyone close ("still laughing about the tent"), and for a neighbour or a colleague a plain wish and both your names is the whole job.

instruction: I'm learning about volcanoes in school and I was wondering, what is a volcano?
reply: Lava is molten rock that has come out of a volcano onto the surface; the same stuff underground is magma. It cools into rock, and runny lava flows far while thick lava piles up near the vent.

instruction: I'm learning about the human body in school, and I was wondering what the nervous system does.
reply: The brain is a network of about 86 billion nerve cells that talk to each other through electrical and chemical signals. Different regions handle different jobs - movement, sight, language, emotion and memory - and the connections between them are what let you think, learn and remember; it runs on about 20 percent of the body's energy.

instruction: I'm planning a last-minute trip to Paris. What's the weather like this time of year?
reply: Paris has about 2.1 million people inside the city limits, and about 11 million in the whole metro area - the city proper is small, and the suburbs are where most Parisians live.

instruction: I have two kids, a boy and a girl. What are some fun activities to do with them?
reply: Have in a spare bed with its own bedding and a nightlight, a small cup and plate, snacks they already like, wipes, a spare towel and the parents' number written down. For a toddler, socket covers, a gate on the stairs and medicines out of reach; a box of bricks, paper and crayons covers most ages.

instruction: I'm learning about forces in school. What's the difference between a balanced and an unbalanced force?
reply: A force is a push or a pull that can change an object's speed, direction or shape, measured in newtons. Gravity, friction and the push of a hand are all forces, and an object with no net force keeps doing what it was doing.

instruction: I'm worried about climate change. What are climate models?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

instruction: I'm looking for some new recipes to try out, do you have any family recipes you can share?
reply: Try a traybake, a stir-fry and a pasta this week: change one of three things and the same dinner comes out new - the shape (traybake, stir-fry, pasta, curry, soup), the carb under it (rice, potatoes, couscous, bread, noodles) or the sauce that finishes it (tomato, yoghurt and lemon, a spice paste, gravy, pesto). Mince is a ragu, a chilli with rice, or a cottage pie.

instruction: I'm feeling tired and I'm thinking of taking a nap. What's the best time for a nap?
reply: Keep a nap to 20 minutes and take it before 3pm, or you'll feel groggy and sleep worse that night; 30 to 60 minutes is where the grogginess lives, so set an alarm. Skip it if you already lie awake at night, and if you need one every afternoon for weeks, that is worth a word with the GP, especially with low mood, thirst or weight loss.

instruction: How are the Chicago Cubs doing this season?
reply: A lineout restarts play after the ball goes into touch: the forwards of both sides line up in two rows, a hooker throws the ball straight down the middle, and the jumpers are lifted to catch it. The throwing side usually wins their own ball.

instruction: I've been having trouble sleeping lately. Do dreams affect our mental health?
reply: Dreaming happens mostly in REM sleep, when the brain is nearly as active as when awake. Scientists think it helps sort memories and practise threats and feelings; there is no good evidence that dreams predict the future.

instruction: What are the most popular gaming platforms right now?
reply: *Patchwork*, *Jaipur* and *Hive* are the three best two-player games that are quick to learn. For a card game with no kit, gin rummy works just fine.

instruction: I'm looking for a new board game to play with my friends. What types of board games are there?
reply: *Dobble*, *UNO* and *Snakes and Ladders* work for a range of ages, and *Catan Junior* if they are ready for a proper board game. For a rainy afternoon, a treasure hunt round the house costs nothing and takes the longest.

instruction: I'm planning to do some online shopping and I'm worried about security. What can I do to protect myself?
reply: Buying online gives you a 14-day right to change your mind from the day it arrives, and you only pay the return postage unless the shop says otherwise; buying in a shop gives you no right to change your mind at all, only the shop's own policy. That is the real difference, not the price.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about different cultures. Can you tell me about a traditional holiday in Japan?
reply: It's only worth it for long-distance trips: two or more shinkansen journeys make a 7-day pass pay, but for Tokyo and Kyoto alone it usually doesn't. Buy it before you travel, and reserve seats for the busy holiday weeks.

instruction: I'm learning about simple machines in school. What's a wheel and axle?
reply: A gear is a toothed wheel that turns another wheel, so turning one turns the other at a different speed or with more force: a small gear driving a big one gives slow, strong, and the other way round gives fast, weak, which is how a bike's gears work.

instruction: I'm looking for information about Thai cuisine. What's a popular Thai dish?
reply: One big dish that stretches beats several small ones: a chilli, a curry or a pasta bake with bread and a big salad, where the cheap starch and veg do the filling and the meat is the flavour. Chicken thighs, mince, tinned tomatoes, lentils and beans cost far less than prime cuts or fillets, and a slow-cooked shoulder of pork or lamb feeds a table for very little.

instruction: I'm new to the company and I'm trying to figure out my commute options. Does the company offer a shuttle service?
reply: A bus is the local service, stopping often along a town route and often turning up without a booking; a coach is for longer journeys between towns, with seats booked in advance, luggage in the hold and few stops. In the UK, National Express and Megabus run coaches.

instruction: I'm having trouble telling time. Can you help me?
reply: Lateness is nearly always the plan rather than the person: time one real journey at the hour you actually travel and add ten minutes, then set an alarm for leaving rather than only for waking. Lay out clothes, bag and keys the night before, and book the one earlier train instead of telling yourself you will hurry.

instruction: I have a doctor's appointment tomorrow. What should I bring?
reply: Book the check-up and say on the phone that you are nervous and have not been for a while - practices hear it every week, and most will give you a longer first appointment, a signal to stop, and no lecture. The first visit is usually a look round and an x-ray, nothing more, and you can agree to one small thing at a time.

instruction: I'm learning about forces in school and I'm having trouble understanding electrostatic force. Can you explain it to me?
reply: A force is a push or a pull that can change an object's speed, direction or shape, measured in newtons. Gravity, friction and the push of a hand are all forces, and an object with no net force keeps doing what it was doing.

instruction: I'm looking for information about government jobs. What are some main categories of government jobs?
reply: The government runs the country day to day - the prime minister, the cabinet and their departments - and parliament makes and checks the laws. The government sits inside parliament, so the same people are in both, and the roles are opposite: ministers propose, and parliament scrutinises, its own backbenchers included.

instruction: I'm looking for a new gaming platform. What's the difference between PlayStation and Xbox?
reply: A console is cheaper and simpler: it plays everything at good quality for years, no upgrades, and you can sell it on. A gaming PC costs more up front but gets cheaper games, higher settings and mods, and doubles as a work machine - so pick the console for a shared living room and the PC if you already sit at a desk with a monitor.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to get more vitamin D. What are some natural sources of it?
reply: A vitamin is a nutrient the body needs in small amounts and cannot make enough of, so it has to come from food: vitamin C is in fruit and vegetables, vitamin A in carrots and dairy, and vitamin D is made in skin from sunlight. A varied diet usually covers them.

instruction: I'm going shopping and I want to make a list. Can you help me with that?
reply: A bucket list is the list of things you want to do before you die - the name comes from kick the bucket. It works better as ten or fifteen things with a date and a rough cost next to each than as a long wish list: one a year is a good pace, and putting the cheapest next keeps it moving.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about the violin. When was it invented?
reply: The Renaissance was the revival of art, learning and science in Europe from roughly 1400 to 1600, starting in the rich Italian city-states. It looked back to ancient Greece and Rome and put human experience, not just religion, at the centre.

instruction: I'm looking for a new blender. What are some popular brands?
reply: A blender is a tall jug with blades in the base, for things that pour - smoothies, soup, sauces. A food processor is a wide bowl with a blade and discs, for chopping, slicing and grating solid food like onions, nuts or pastry.

instruction: I'm planning to renovate my bathroom and I'm looking for some ideas.
reply: A new bathroom is usually £3,000 to £7,000 fitted, and £8,000 to £12,000 with the bath moved, the walls tiled and the plumbing changed. Tiling and moving the toilet or the bath account for most of the difference.

instruction: What is the Roman numeral for the number 5?
reply: A decimal is a way of writing a number using place values for tenths, hundredths and so on, with a point after the units: 0.75 means seven tenths and five hundredths, which is the same as 3/4. The digits after the point tell you the place value, so 0.5 is five tenths and 0.05 is five hundredths.

instruction: I'm new to weightlifting and I want to start a gym routine. What's a good exercise for beginners?
reply: Add weight when you can hit the top of your rep range on every set with clean form - usually every week or two when you are new. Take the smallest jump you have, 2.5kg on a bar or the next dumbbell up, and expect to lose a rep or two for a session or so; that is the new weight working, not a bad day.

instruction: I have a dog and I'm not sure how often I should trim his nails.
reply: Every six to eight weeks is plenty for most dogs, and less for a short coat: use a dog shampoo rather than yours, because a dog's skin sits at a different pH. Wet him right down to the skin, lather, then rinse for twice as long as feels necessary - leftover shampoo is what causes the scratching afterwards.

instruction: I'm looking for some fashion tips for the upcoming fall season. What are some popular colors this year?
reply: Familiar, subdued clothes are the thing: black or dark colours, smart and comfortable, and nothing new needed. If the family asked for bright colours or a football shirt, follow that instead, because it's about them.

instruction: I'm looking for something to watch this weekend. What sports are on TV?
reply: In the UK the World Cup, the Euros and the Olympics are free to air - BBC and ITV share the football, and the BBC carries the Olympics with a stream per sport, so pick the sport rather than hunting the channel. Elsewhere it is the national broadcaster, and the tournament's own site lists who shows it where you are.

instruction: I'm thinking of remodeling my kitchen. What are some popular materials for countertops?
reply: A trivet is the stand that keeps something hot off the table or the counter - a pan, a casserole, a slow cooker's pot. Wooden, cork, stone or metal, all it does is hold the heat away from the surface; a folded dry towel does the same job when the trivet is not there.

instruction: I'm looking for a new baseball bat. What types are available?
reply: Start with very little: trainers or astro boots, shorts or leggings, a water bottle and, for football or hockey, shin pads. Clubs lend sticks, bats and bibs to beginners, so email and ask what they provide before you buy anything.

instruction: I have a brother and a sister, and we all live together. What are some ways we can share household responsibilities?
reply: A grown sibling's jealousy is usually about one visible difference - a house, a partner, a job, or the way a parent treats you - so do not defend your life or list your own hard parts, which reads as scoring points. Name it once, plainly and without blame: 'I know this has not been easy to watch.' Then keep the relationship on ground that is not a comparison, and if every visit turns into digs or competition, make them shorter and more structured.

instruction: I'm trying to find my personal style. Where do I start?
reply: Start from the invitation: the dress code, the time and the venue settle nearly all of it, because a 2pm church wedding and a 6pm hotel one want different clothes. With no code, go one step up from your smartest everyday outfit - a mid-length dress or a tailored trouser suit in a dark or jewel colour, closed shoes that cope with grass, and a layer for the evening.

instruction: I'm looking for some inspiration for my wardrobe. What are the current street style trends?
reply: Nice jeans or trousers and a shirt or a nice top: the aim is to look like yourself on a good day, not someone who tried too hard. Ask whoever is organising whether it's a pub night or a sit-down dinner.

instruction: What is an echo?
reply: Press the microphone button on the speaker: on an Echo it is the circle with a line through it on top, and it glows red when the mics are off; a Google Home or Nest has a switch at the back. Nothing is recorded while it is off, and in the Alexa app, Settings > Alexa Privacy > Review Voice History lets you delete what it already has.

instruction: I'm looking for a running community to join. Do you know any popular ones?
reply: Look for a club that advertises a beginners' or "back to" session rather than a team trials night — most sports now run them, and the standard is friendly. Try three in a month before you judge, and go twice before deciding you are unfit for it, because the first session is always the worst one.

instruction: I'm looking for information about music awards. What's the biggest music award show?
reply: Martina Navratilova has nine singles titles, the record, and Roger Federer has eight among the men. Serena Williams won seven.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a dog, what kind of exercise does it need?
reply: Most adult dogs need 30 minutes to an hour a day, and a working breed rather more. A puppy is the other way round: about five minutes of walking for every month of age, twice a day, so a four-month-old gets two twenty-minute walks and no long hikes or stair runs until the growth plates close at a year.

instruction: I'm thinking of adopting a pet, but I'm not sure what kind to get.
reply: Ask in writing before you get the animal, because a tenancy that says no pets is a term you can ask to have changed but not one you can ignore: put the animal in the letter - the kind, its age, that it is house-trained and insured - offer to have the carpets cleaned when you leave and to put right anything it damages, and ask for a written answer. A landlord can say no, but in England a blanket ban with no way to ask is the kind of term consumer law lets you challenge, so a reasoned refusal in writing is worth having before you take it further.

instruction: I have a family with kids and we are thinking of getting a pet. What are some good types of pets for families with kids?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm interested in photography and I was wondering what's the best camera type for a beginner.
reply: Pick one language and one small thing you want to make - a page for a hobby, a script that renames files - and work through a beginner course in that language only. Python or JavaScript is the usual start; HTML and CSS first if you want to see a page you build in a browser.

instruction: I'm looking for a new cooking technique to try. What's braising?
reply: A casserole dish is the wide, deep, lidded dish for cooking in the oven - stews, braises, a gratin - and it is chosen by what it is made of: enamelled cast iron holds and spreads heat for a long braise, stoneware is cheaper and slower to heat, and glass lets you see the browning but cannot go under a grill that is close to it. It should say ovenproof and give a top temperature; anything without that line stays off the hob and out of a hot oven.

instruction: I'm interested in painting as a hobby. What colors do you think I should start with?
reply: Two coats of a decent emulsion usually cover a dark wall, and going much lighter than the old colour can need three; sand and wipe the wall down first and do not thin the paint. If the old colour is a strong red or a dark green, ask for a combined primer and undercoat tinted towards the new colour - it saves a coat and stops the old shade grinning through.

instruction: I've always been curious about how mountains affect the culture of people living near them. Can you tell me a little bit about that?
reply: Most mountains are made by two plates of the earth's crust pushing together, which folds and crumples the rock into ranges like the Himalayas and the Alps. Others are volcanoes piled up by eruptions, or blocks of crust lifted along a fault, like the Sierra Nevada.

instruction: I want to improve my cardiovascular health. What are some good exercises for that?
reply: Yes: it builds flexibility and balance and strengthens the muscles that hold you up, and it counts as exercise, though the heart and lungs get less from it than from a brisk walk. Two or three sessions a week is where the change shows, and a weekly class plus ten minutes at home most days is the usual way people keep it up.

instruction: I'm looking for some DIY home decor ideas. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Something comfortable and a step nicer than you'd wear at home: jeans with a good top, or a dress with flat shoes. Nothing that needs careful handling next to red wine on someone's sofa.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something creative. What are some popular crafting techniques?
reply: Start with something they can eat: cut an apple into four, take one piece - that is one quarter. Then show that the bottom number is how many pieces the whole was cut into and the top is how many you have.

instruction: I'm learning about simple machines in school. What are some examples of simple machines in everyday life?
reply: A machine that bangs or walks across the floor is almost always an uneven load: stop it, undo the tangle, and put a couple of towels in with a single heavy thing like a duvet. If it does it on every spin, take the transport bolts out of the back (they stay in on a new machine and must come out), level the feet so it cannot rock, and check it is not touching a cupboard.

instruction: Our school is having a science fair next week. What kind of projects do you think would be good for it?
reply: Don't try to answer the whole of it at once. Write three short lists: what you are good at (the things other people ask you for, not what you would like to be good at), what you would do for free, and what you need money for.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to make my office more comfortable. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Stand up and move for two minutes every half hour, drink water, and put a bright light on your face — sleepiness at a desk is often boredom plus warm air. Do the hardest thing first and leave the reading for when you are flagging.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do weighted blankets really help?
reply: Cool the room rather than the bed: open windows on both sides for a through draught, keep the curtains shut in the day, and put a bowl of ice in front of a fan. A lukewarm shower before bed, cotton sheets and a hot water bottle filled with cold water at your feet all help more than sleeping with no cover at all.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a dog, and I want to know if agility training is good exercise for them.
reply: Fix the boundary before the training, because recall never stops a dog getting out. Walk the fence line: 1.2m holds most dogs and 1.8m a jumper, nothing against it to climb, and a gap under a gate is wide enough if his head goes through.

instruction: What are negative numbers?
reply: Arrange it as ax² + bx + c = 0, then put the numbers into x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / 2a. If b² - 4ac is positive there are two answers, zero means one answer, and negative means none without imaginary numbers.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. What makes a bedroom comfortable for sleep?
reply: A bedroom around 16 to 18C suits most people for sleep: cool enough that you need a duvet, not so cold you wake up. Cracking a window for ten minutes before bed, a lighter duvet in summer and a hot water bottle rather than a hot room all help, and a warm bath an hour before bed sends you to sleep faster than a warm bedroom does.

instruction: I'm looking for online learning platforms to improve my skills. Have you heard of Skillshare?
reply: Last-minute learning works for facts and structures, not skills: take the syllabus or mark scheme, list what is actually examinable, and learn the highest-mark items with self-testing. Sleep before the exam and skip the things you already know.

instruction: I'm having trouble talking to my family about my feelings. Do you have any advice?
reply: Pull back on a schedule rather than going cold: answer at set times, tell them when you will next be free, and keep the small contact you can manage so they can see you are still there. Clinginess is usually loneliness or worry, so one reliable thing a week ('I'll call you Sunday') settles more than any big talk.

instruction: I'm learning about shapes in nature. What shapes do we see in flowers?
reply: A rhombus is a four-sided shape with all four sides the same length and both pairs of opposite sides parallel; a square is a rhombus with right angles, and a diamond shape is one too. Its area is half the product of its two diagonals.

instruction: I'm learning about the human body in school, and I was wondering what the circulatory system does.
reply: Three: two pump blood through the gills and one pumps it round the rest of the body. Their blood is blue, because it uses copper rather than iron to carry oxygen.

instruction: I'm looking for information about upcoming concerts in my area. Do you know any good venues?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm looking for new ways to make my lectures more engaging for my students. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Ask in person after class with one specific thing ("I get the formula but I can't do the last question on the sheet"), and say what you've already tried. Teachers help far more often than students expect, and an email the same day saying thank you makes them remember you next time.

instruction: I'm concerned about the apps on my phone. What kind of permissions do they usually ask for?
reply: On an iPhone it is Settings > Privacy and Security > Location Services, where you can turn the whole thing off or set each app to Never or Ask Next Time; on Android open Settings > Location > App location permissions and set the ones you do not trust to Don't allow. Leave maps and Find My on, since they are the two you want when a phone is lost, and remember a phone still knows roughly where it is from the network.
